# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary | 2026-07-29

The US equities duopoly remains dominant: Nasdaq 100 leads decisively with 0.0025% per $1M ILLIQ and 0.7631% AR spread, while NYSE follows with 0.0061% per $1M ILLIQ despite a tighter 0.6465% spread. Tokyo Stock Exchange anchors the second tier with 0.0361% per $1M ILLIQ and notably high 2.7810% turnover ratio, reflecting concentrated trading activity. Euronext, SIX Swiss, Xetra, Hong Kong, and London form a fragmented mid-pack, all exceeding 0.0302% per $1M ILLIQ; notably, Euronext offers the tightest 0.5167% spread among this cohort but maintains middling 0.5932% turnover, signaling tight microprice discovery alongside modest participation. Korea Exchange emerges as a significant outlier, with the widest 1.6160% AR spread and highest 0.1483% per $1M ILLIQ despite reasonable 1.1028% turnover ratio—a rare metric divergence indicating structural execution costs that turnover alone cannot explain. London Stock Exchange rounds out the bottom with 0.0828% per $1M ILLIQ and modest $10.6M comparable volume, limiting its practical utility for large cross-border allocations.
